guard: the events plane does not republish TOOL_CALL_ARGS or TOOL_CALL_RESULT, including on AguiEmitter.start recovery of a frozen pre-fix body, and a frozen body whose event list cannot be read is withheld rather than published opaque; six carriers fail independently; sibling text still publishes
why: THE COORDINATE IS THE RECORDED PUBLISH. FakeEndpoint.multicastExpecting is what the broker would
have been handed. The mapper return is upstream of recover()'s bypass. The WAL body is frozen
pre-policy by design. A cell on either of those would pass with the defect wide open. That is why
PR #1415's two mutation kills proved the suite depended on the mutated lines rather than that a
live entry point reached them. This fixture's recover mutation is the one #1415 lacked: it drives
AguiEmitter.start() against a sent_unacked TOOL_CALL_RESULT body.
CONNECTOR-CORE EXPORTS RESOLVE TO dist/. The command AND each mutation's afterRestore rebuild, or
the mutant is read by nothing and a poisoned dist survives the restore.
SIX CARRIERS ARE SIX CELLS. A mutation that reopens only ARGS must red an args cell, not a shared
'no marks' cell. T-ARGS deletes TOOL_CALL_ARGS from the forbidden set; T-RESULT deletes
TOOL_CALL_RESULT; T-RETRY deletes the attempt() refusal.
T-ARGS/T-RESULT/T-RETRY are all MORE PERMISSIVE, so they cannot grade liveness. T-LIVENESS adds
TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT to the forbidden set and must red the sibling-text cell. That is the decoy
that proves the suite would notice if the policy started refusing everything. A TOOL_CALL_START
decoy is not used: dropping START makes END fail the batch validator, so the first red would be
the channel-control cell (empty publish) rather than a START/END control.
